slides.text: Do what you'd do with a paper dictionary: open the middle, keep one half, ignore the other.
mid = 7 < 9 → everything up to 7 is too small. Gone.
slides.alt: The sorted list 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 with 1 to 5 dimmed and 7 ringed; lo sits on 9 and hi on 13: mid = 7 < 9 → drop 7 and everything left of it.

slides.text: mid = 11 > 9 → 11 and everything after it. Gone.
slides.alt: The same list with only 9 still lit and 11 ringed; lo and hi both on 9: mid = 11 > 9 → drop 11 and everything right.
9 ringed with lo and hi on it: mid = 9 → found in 3 checks.

slides.text: Each check halves the range: O(log n).
slides.alt: Python binary_search(arr, target): lo, hi = 0, len(arr) - 1; while lo <= hi: mid = lo + (hi - lo) // 2, returning mid on a match, lo = mid + 1 when arr[mid] < target, else hi = mid - 1; return -1. The else branch is highlighted with the note "Too big: move hi below mid"; on the list, 11 > 9 → hi = 4.

slides.text: A million sorted numbers take at most 20 checks. A billion, 30.
slides.alt: "1,000,000 sorted numbers": check 20 leaves at most 1, so at most 20 checks; 1,000,000,000 → at most 30.

slides.text: The classic bug: lo = mid instead of mid + 1. Search [1, 3] for 3: mid stays 0 and lo stays 0, forever.
slides.alt: "The classic bug": lo = mid + 1 ✓ against lo = mid ✗. On [1, 3], find 3: lo = 0, hi = 1, mid = 0; 1 < 3 → lo = mid = 0 … again, forever.
